3. It is the contention of the writ petitioners although their service records are better and that they are also senior to the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 but they have not been promoted and thus they have been deprived of their right to get promotion as Section Officer, that the Board, promoted the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 in an arbitrary manner since the service records of the said respondents are bad and that they are also junior to the writ petitioners, that the action of the Board is violative of the Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution. The writ petitioners contended that they were selected by the Selection Committee (the assertion is not correct) but the Board illegally did not consider the recommendation of the Selection Committee, that as per service regulation 5(a) of the Board regulating the service of the employees of the Board, the Board was required to give promotion on the basis of seniority but the said criteria was given a go-by in the case of the writ petitioners. 

 4. Appellants (respondent Nos. 1 and 2 in the writ petition) contested the Rule by filing affidavit- in-opposition denying the material averments made in the writ petition and stating, inter alia, that a meeting of the Selection Committee of the Board was held on 25-11-1997 for the purpose of recommending names of employees from amongst the Listed employees of the Board for promotion to the post of Section Officer and other post, that for the purpose of promotion to the post of Section Officer and other equivalent post a list of 29 Upper Division Assistants was prepared in order of seniority with the necessary information and comments against their names and the same was placed before the Selection Committee, that the Selection Committee on consideration of the information and comments in the list of the employees prepared list of 12 employees, of whom 11 for promotion to the post of Section Officer and one as Accountant, that in due course the list so prepared by the Selection Committee for promotion to the post of Section Officer was placed before the Board and the Board in its meeting held on 24-12-1997 on consideration of the materials before it dropped one of the selected candidates i.e. Md Sirajul Islam, who was selected for promotion as Section Officer, because of adverse comments in the service record and also being punished and in his place name of the respondent No. 3 was listed for promotion to the post of Section Officer and the Board finally approved the promotion of the 11 Upper Division Assistants as Section Officer and one as an Accountant, that although respondent No. 4 appeared in the SSC examination as a student of night section without obtaining prior permission from the Board but the Board finally exonerated him for not obtaining prior permission in appearing in the SSC examination, that as to correction of the date of birth or, in other words, age of the respondent No, 4 the Board on consideration of the materials placed before it allowed the representation of the respondent No.4 and thereupon date of birth of respondent No. 4 was recorded as 28-3-1948, that amendment of the date of birth of the respondent No, 4 was not done by him in derogation of any. of the Rules, rather the said amendment was allowed by the Board, that as there was adverse remark in the service record of the writ petitioner No. 1 (herein respondent No.1) as to registration matters and the writ petitioner No. 2 (respondent No. 2 herein) was under suspension because of being an accused in two criminal cases the Selection Committee did not consider their case for promotion to the post of Section Officer; that respondent No.4 was selected by the Selection Committee for promotion and the Board approved the same, that in case writ petitioners get promotion then the respondent No. 4 would not be deprived from promotion as per seniority since at the same time the next 5 other employees would get promotion and, as such, there was no illegality in selecting the two respondents for promotion to the post of Section Officer and finally promoting them as Section Officer, that although the writ petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 are senior to the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 but the service record of the writ petitioner No. 1 is not clean, rather there is adverse comment and that writ petitioner No.2 was placed under suspension being accused in criminal cases and for those reasons although they are senior but their case for promotion has not been considered and, as 'such, there was no violation of Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution in not promoting them. 

 5. The undisputed position is that at the time when the Selection Committee was considering case of 29 employees for the purpose of promotion to the post of Section Officer and the other equivalent post the respondent No.2 was under suspension being accused in two criminal cases and the respondent No.1 by the office Memo dated 18-11-1995 was given warning for illegal activities relating to registration. 

 7. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute with the observation "On a reference to the Rules for Disciplinary Action against the officers and employees of the Board, we do not find any bar or restriction for consideration for promotion of an employee for reasons assigned in the case of the two petitioners". The High Court Division further observed on consideration of the Rules for Disciplinary Action "we could not lay our hands of any prohibition for consideration as to promotion if the employee happens to be under suspension or there is a warning against hum. These are not covered by penalties enumerated in Rule 1(r) and (vi) of the Rules of Disciplinary Action against the officers and employees of the Board. " 

 8. It also appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division considered the submission made from the side of the writ petitioners that order of suspension being not a punishment the case of the respondent No.2 ought to have been considered before taking the case of respondent Nos. 3 and 4 for consideration for promotion to the post of Section Officer. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute upon observing "Regard being had to the discussion made above, and for the foregoing reasons we are convinced that the petitioners have been able to make out a case to get a declaration from this court that Annexure E is liable to be declared so far the same relates to the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect." 

 9. Leave was obtained for the consideration of the submissions that the High Court Division was in error in holding that there was no bar in considering the case of promotion of an employee while he is under suspension or against whom earlier serious warning was recorded in his service book, although the recognised rule is otherwise and, as such, judgment and order of the High Court Division is not legally sustainable, that in the matter of promotion mere seniority is not a sole criterion and, as such, High Court Division was in error in taking exception to the order of promotion so far the same relates to respondent Nos. 3 and 4 on the ground they were junior to the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 i.e. the writ petitioners. 

 10. At the time of granting leave it was submitted by the learned Counsel entering caveat for the respondent No.1, that although Selection Committee in its meeting held on 25-11-1997 made decision that the case of promotion of respondent No.1 would be considered in a subsequent meeting but the Board in its meeting held on 24-12-1997 while considering the recommendation of the Selection Committee without considering the case of the respondent No.1 selected respondent No.3 for promotion to the post of Section Officer and made final his promotion to the said post in spite of there being no recommendation from the Selection Committee for respondent No. 3's promotion as Section Officer and thus unjustly deprived the respondent No. 1 of his entitlement of being promoted to the post of Section Officer. 

 11. The learned Advocate-on-Record for the appellants submits that the High Court Division was in error in holding that there is no provision in the Service Regulation that while an employee is under suspension or that there is adverse remark in the service record of an employee, that is, he was warned for illegal activities in the matter of registration, to exclude his case from consideration while case of promotion of the employees of the said category is taken for consideration by the Selection Committee in that the accepted practice is that when an employee is under suspension begin an accused in criminal cases (as the case of respondent No.2) his case of promotion is kept in abeyance till clearance from the criminal case and that in case of the employee in whose service record there is adverse remark that he was warned for resorting to illegal activities in the matter of registration the Committee while considering the case of promotion of the employees of the said group is quite competent to leave out the case of such category from consideration for promotion to the higher post or may take some other decision as in the instant case that case of promotion of respondent No. 1 would be considered in the next meeting. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Advocate- on-Record, the learned Counsel for the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 submits that warning being not a punishment the Selection Committee was not correct in leaving out the case of respondent No. 1 from consideration for promotion. 

 12. The respondent No.1 was warned for his being engaged in illegal activities relating to registration and the noting so made in the service record may not be a punishment in its strict sense but undoubtedly, being reprimand in the background of the conduct demonstrated by the respondent No. 1 and the same certainly is a stigma in the service record. In such a situation, in our view, the Selection Committee did not act either in arbitrary manner or illegally in leaving out for the time being the case of the respondent No.1 while considering the case of promotion of the other employees of respondent No. 1's category. 

 13. The learned Counsel, in support of the submission that except a warning noted in service record of the said respondent No. 1 there was nothing else for leaving out his case from consideration for promotion and upon placing reliance on Rule 4 of the Service Rules relating to the conditions of service of the employees of the Board providing penalties, submits since warning is not punishment the authority acted arbitrarily in not considering respondent No.1 for promotion. It is seen from Rule 4 that warning has not been listed as punishment but the fact remains that the respondent No.1 was warned for his illegal activities relating to registration and the same was noted in his service record and this shows that the service record of the respondent was not clean or, in other words, not free from blame. This being the position we are of the view the Selection Committee did not act either arbitrarily or unreasonably in not considering the case of the respondent No. 1 for promotion for the time being. 

 14. It is the contention of the learned Counsel for the respondent No.1 that Selection Committee in its meeting held on 25-11-1997 postponed the case of respondent No. 1 upon taking decision to consider his case in the subsequent meeting relating to the matter of promotion of the employees and that the Board while taking decision as to the persons who were recommended by the Selection Committee for promotion and that while dropped the name of one of such persons i.e. Md Sirajul Islam, who was recommended for promotion as Section Officer, the Board ought to have considered the case of respondent No. 1 and having had not done so the Board acted arbitrarily and unreasonably. The contention so made appears to be not well founded since the Board in all matters is not bound by the decision of the Selection Committee. Moreover, as has earlier been mentioned that respondent No. 1 was warned for resorting to illegal activities relating to registration and this shows that respondent No.1 although senior to the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 but he was lacking integrity and honesty and that being the situation it cannot be said that the Board acted arbitrarily and unreasonably in not considering the case of the respondent No. 1 while upon dropping the name of one of the employees who was recommended for promotion by the Selection Committee and thereupon considered the case of other employees including the respondent No.3. 

 15. The contention on behalf of the respondent No.2 is that although respondent No.2 was under suspension but there is nothing in the Rules relating to service condition of the employees of the Board, that an employee while under suspension, his case would not be taken up for consideration for promotion till he is cleared or that order of suspension is recalled or withdrawn. Further contention is that since at the time of disposal of the writ petition the respondent No.2 was cleared from the criminal cases in connection with which he was placed under suspension the High Court Division did not commit any error in giving direction for promoting the respondent No.2. It may be mentioned that the High Court Division although declared the office order as in Annexure E to the writ petition to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect so far the same relates to the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 but at the same time further declared that in case the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are promoted and placed above the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 in that case the declaration so made would not adversely effect the promotion of respondent Nos. 3 and 4. 

 16. The contention of the respondent No.2 that since he was cleared of the criminal cases while the writ petition was decided or disposed of and thereby he was entitled to be promoted as directed by the High Court Division appears to be not legally well founded, since acquittal in a criminal case ipso facto does not entitle one to promotion being senior to those who have been already promoted as the case of promotion of a particular employee is processed through different stages to reach finality. 

 17. The accepted principle is that seniority alone does not create right to promotion and that some other factors like sincerity, honesty, integrity, efficiency, character, sense of value, etc. are taken into consideration in the case of promotion. This being the accepted principle it is for the authority to make decision as regard the matter of promotion of a particular employee like respondent No.2 and, as such, the Court would not be within its jurisdiction in making direction to an authority to promote a particular employee and thereby depriving the authority from considering the case of promotion of an employee in the background of the facts available to it. It is within the domain of the authority to make decision in the matter of promotion of its employees in the background of the facts available as well as upon due compliance of Rule/Regulation, if any, and then if the decision so made is challenged, it would be quite within the jurisdiction of the Court to examine whether in arriving at the decision the authority has complied with the requirements of Rule/Regulation or that has taken into consideration extraneous matter or failed to take into consideration matter (s) which ought to have been taken into consideration or that the authority proceeded on flawed procedure and material or left out material which was very much integral to matter of promotion process. 

 19. The learned Counsel for the respondent contends that in the absence of recommendation by the Selection Committee the Board is not competent to promote any employee. This contention is not legally sound since there is nothing in the Rule that the promotion of the employees of the Board can only be made on the basis of the recommendation of a Selection Committee or, in other words, the Board while considering the recommendation of the Selection Committee in case finds one or more of the recommended employee or employees not eligible for promotion is not competent to consider case of employee left out by the Selection Committee and take decision to promote an employee and finally, to make order for promotion. In the Rules regulating service condition of the employees of the Board it is provided that ordinarily appointment of the employees of the Board except the Chairman shall be advertised and the Board shall make the appointment after obtaining the recommendation of the Selection Committee. There is nothing in the Rule precluding the Board from scrutinizing and examining the recommendation of the Selection Committee for promotion and that to drop the name of an employee recommended by the Selection Committee and in the place of the employee so dropped to select someone who is otherwise found eligible for promotion and this being the position selection of the respondent No.3 dropping the name of Md Sirajul Islam, whose name was recommended by the Selection Committee for promotion as Section Officer, because of the blemish service record, i.e. he was punished, while the Board considering the recommendation of the Selection Committee, the Board did not act arbitrarily or unreasonably. 

 20. The learned Counsel submits that the Selection Committee in its meeting held on 25-11-1997 took decision that case of promotion of respondent No. 1 would be considered in the next meeting and, as such, the Board while selected respondent No.3 ought to have considered the case of respondent No. 1 and having had not done so the High Court Division did not commit any error in declaring that promotion of respondent No. 3 to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect. As regard the decision of the Selection Committee in respect of respondent No.1 as noted hereinbefore, suffice it to say that case of said respondent would be considered later on by the Selection Committee while there would be an occasion for consideration of the matter of promotion of the employees. The Board while considering recommendation of the Selection Committee, wherein undisputedly the name of the respondents were not, found one of the recommended employees i.e. Md Sirajul Islam, not fit for promotion because of punishment awarded and then considered the case of the other employees who are otherwise fit to be considered for promotion and considering the seniority and other criteria of promotion the Board considered respondent No.3 eligible for promotion and thereupon took decision to promote him as Section Officer. The learned Counsel submits that when the Board promoted respondent No.3 taking his seniority into consideration, the Board ought to have considered the case of the respondent No. 1 who is senior to the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 and that having had not done so acted arbitrarily in selecting the respondent Nos. 3 and 4. It may be mentioned that Selection Committee recommended name of respondent No.4 for promotion as Section Officer. The contention of the learned Counsel that respondent No. 1 being senior to the respondent No. 3 the Board acted arbitrarily and unreasonably in promoting the respondent No. 3 is not well founded, since the Board was not precluded or otherwise not incompetent to consider the case of the respondent No.3 in the background of the service record of the respondent No.1. 

 21. The learned Counsel upon referring to the Rules relating to manner of appointment of the employees of the Board submits that therein it has been provided that promotion shall be made on the basis of efficiency and seniority in the service and that respondent Nos. 1 and 2 being undeniably senior to the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 the Board acted arbitrarily in not promoting the respondent Nos. 1 and 2. It has already been mentioned that while the matter of promotion of the listed employees to the post of Section Officer was considered respondent No.2 was under suspension being accused in criminal cases and that there was remark in the service record of the respondent No.1 that he was warned for his illegal activities in the matter of registration. In that state of the matter, although the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are senior to the respondent Nos. 3 and 4, the Selection Committee and, for that matter, the Board did not act in arbitrary manner in not making decision to promote the said employees and consequently, it cannot be said that promotion of the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 was made without lawful authority or, in other words, was not legal. 

 22. In support of the submission that in the absence of recommendation of the Selection Committee the Board was not competent to take decision to promote any person to any post and, a such, promotion of the respondent Nos. 3 being arbitrary the High Court Division did not commit any error in declaring promotion of the respondent No.3 illegal and to have been made without lawful authority, the learned Counsel has not referred any Rule, Regulation or law. It is seen from the Rules relating to service conditions of the employees of the Board that ordinarily appointment of the officers other than Chairman is to be made by the Board after obtaining recommendation of the Selection Committee. This provision in no way can be stretched to the case of promotion of the employees of the Board. This being the position we are of the view the Board is quite competent to consider the case of a particular employee for promotion, as in the instant case as regard respondent No.3 in the absence of recommendation of Selection Committee, and that if the Board is of the view, in the background of the materials before it, that a particular person is eligible then the Board is very much competent to promote him to a particular post The learned Counsel has also submitted that in the absence of any provision in the Service Rule if the authority does not consider the case of an employee for promotion because of being under suspension or pendency of criminal case then the authority acts in an arbitrary manner. The submission appears to be of no merit, since the accepted practice and procedure is that when a person is under suspension either in connection with departmental proceeding or of being an accused in a criminal case, his case for promotion is not taken up for consideration during that period and this practice is based on prudence and that if at a later stage he is cleared and promoted then his seniority is maintained upon following with the next below post practice i.e. he is put at a place where he would have been if his case would have been considered earlier, had he not been under suspension, along with those who have already been promoted. 

 23. The learned Counsel in support of his submission that promotion can be made upon effecting the same retrospectively has referred to the case of Government of India and another vs CA Balakrishnan and others reported in AIR 1975 SC 1498. We find no reason to differ with the view expressed in the reported case that in case of employees whose case have been left out of consideration for promotion on misconception of law or fact or on untenable ground and if the decision is challenged and the Court upon declaring the decision so made illegal make direction for consideration of the case of the person so left out taking the position on the date when he was so left out and that if such person is found to be fit for promotion on that day on which day he was left out in that case promotion of such person would take effect back to the date on which he was left out of consideration and that others were promoted. We have also been referred to the case of Ram Sewak Prasad vs State of UP and others reported in AIR 1991 SC 1818 wherein it has been held, in the state of matter as noted before, the promotion of such employee did take back promotion with the benefit. The learned Counsel upon referring to the Rules making provision that promotion of the employees shall be on the basis of efficiency and seniority and that contending the Board having had violated the said provision as regard respondent Nos. 1 and 2 submits that the High Court Division was not in error in declaring the promotion of respondent Nos. 3 and 4 to have been made without lawful authority and in support thereof has referred to the case of ANM Belayet Hossain and others vs Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation reported in 51 DLR 104. It is seen from the report that the respondent- organization’s provision relating to promotion was that promotion would be made keeping in view of the Rule of merit and the Rule of seniority but the respondent-organisation made promotion of its employees giving go-by to the said provision i.e. merit-cum-seniority but by applying the rule of merit only and in the aforesaid state of the matter promotion of the employees was declared to have been made without lawful authority. The facts and circumstances of the case referred by the learned Counsel is quite different from the facts and circumstances of the instant case. In our opinion, the Board is no! .precluded, although in the Rule there is Rule of seniority and efficiency, from leaving out the case of employees as the case of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 from consideration while considering the case of promotion of its employees. Petition for leave to appeal against the judgment of the said reported case was disposed of in the light of agreement arrived at by the parties [4 BLC (AD) 65]. The learned Counsel, in support of his contention that although seniority is not the lone criteria for promotion but by virtue of seniority one has right to be considered for promotion, has referred to the case of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Communications, Road and Road Transport Division and another vs Md Azizur Rahman and others reported in 46 DLR (AD) 19 wherein it has been observed "Seniority is of course a term and condition of service but, as has been pointed out above, seniority is determined by set principles or statutory rules; the order of seniority may also be altered by such rules. Ordinarily, alteration of seniority does not curtail the right to future appointment, that is, promotion. Promotion is not a matter of right; it is to be earned by meritorious service which includes efficiency, good conduct, character and integrity, dynamic personality and, above all, sense of value and proportion. Seniority alone is not sufficient for promotion but it is certainly one of the primary requisites for promotion. Though by seniority alone a person cannot earn promotion, he, by virtue of seniority, has a right to be considered for promotion". We are fully in agreement with the view expressed in the aforesaid case. 

 24. The settled principle of law is that seniority alone is not the sole basis for promotion and that seniority does not create a claim for being promoted although the same creates a right in favour of an employee to consider his case of promotion along with the case of others who are posted in the similar situation. Promotion is to be earned by rendering meritorious service and other than seniority promotion is also conditioned by other factors, such as efficiency, good conduct, character, integrity, sense of value, honesty and temperamental suitability.
